turns: I have a two-year work permit in Sweden. What salary does my job need to pay?
question: And can my spouse come here and work too?
reference_answer: Yes, normally. Your spouse or partner can be granted a residence permit tied to your work permit under 4 kap. 4 a § utlänningsförordningen, if you can support yourself and your spouse; exceptions for special reasons. The level is set in 4 kap. 4 c §: salary after preliminary tax of at least the protected amount for wage garnishment, counting the spouse too (when the permit is later extended, the spouse's own income and that of others in the household also count). The permit is valid for the same period as yours. With a temporary residence permit your spouse may also be given a work permit (6 kap. 3 § utlänningslagen); Migrationsverket's page says adult family members are permitted to work. The salary question from the earlier turn does not need to be answered again.

Same facts as family-spouse-004 (corrected 2026-11-24). Reviewed 2026-11-24 on the review page. turns: I've had work permits in Sweden for four and a half years. Can I get permanent residence?
question: What else do I need besides the time?
reference_answer: Besides four years with a permit for work during the last seven (5 kap. 5 § utlänningslagen), permanent residence requires that you can support yourself and that, given your expected conduct, there is no doubt it should be granted (5 kap. 7 §). The ordinance sets the support level: salary after preliminary tax of at least the protected amount for wage garnishment, counting only yourself, with a certain permanence; income from a business also counts, unemployment benefits do not (4 kap. 4 e § utlänningsförordningen). Migrationsverket's page adds that you must have met the conditions of your work permits and actually worked in Sweden during the four years. Exceptions for special reasons are in 5 kap. 8 §.

turns: I'm in Sweden on a work permit, and my employer has just told me my job ends at the end of the month.
question: How long do I have, and does the time start now or when the job ends?
reference_answer: The permit may be revoked when the employment has ended, unless within three months you get a new job covered by the permit, or apply for a work permit for a new job and that application is later granted (7 kap. 3 § första stycket 2 utlänningslagen). It is a 'may', not an automatic expiry. Migrationsverket counts the three months from the last day of employment, not from when notice is given. The three months do not extend your permit: they apply only while it is still valid. A new job may need a new work-permit application, depending on the employer and on whether the permit is limited to a profession.

turns: My work permit was granted in February 2026.
question: I'm registering my extension application this week. What salary will I need?
reference_answer: Because the permit was granted before 1 June 2026 and the extension is registered with Migrationsverket by 1 December 2026, the older wording of 6 kap. 2 § första stycket 1 utlänningslagen applies (transitional provision 2 to SFS 2026:295; the same for the ordinance in SFS 2026:605): the employment must give good maintenance (god försörjning), which the ordinance (5 kap. 8 a § utlänningsförordningen in its older wording) defined as a salary of at least 80 percent of the median salary published by Statistics Sweden; Migrationsverket states this as at least SEK 30,640 a month before tax. 1 December 2026 is the last registration date: an extension registered from 2 December falls under the new requirement of at least 90 percent of the median salary. Salary, insurance and other terms must still be no worse than Swedish collective agreements or practice in the profession or industry.

turns: I have a work permit tied to my current employer, and another company has offered me a job.
question: Do I apply for a new permit or an extension before I start there?
reference_answer: Your permit is tied to your current employer, so you need a work permit for the new job before you work there. Migrationsverket's page calls this a new work-permit application; in law it is an extension with a new employment (6 kap. 4 a § utlänningslagen: the new job must meet 2 § första stycket and also andra stycket), and in Migrationsverket's e-service it is made through the extension route while your current permit is valid. You can start working for the new employer once you have applied, before the decision, provided you applied before your current permit expired; the new employer must have advertised the job in Sweden and the EU/EEA and Switzerland first.

turns: I'm here on a work permit, and my spouse has a family permit tied to mine but doesn't work.
question: When I get permanent residence, can my spouse get it too?
reference_answer: Possibly, but normally not without an income of their own. You and your spouse can apply for permanent residence at the same time; Migrationsverket assesses your application first and, if you are granted permanent residence, then your spouse's. Your spouse can then be granted permanent residence when the permit expires if they have had a temporary permit for at least three years, the conditions for a family permit under 5 kap. 3 a § are met — which brings your own maintenance and housing requirement as the person in Sweden (5 kap. 3 j §) — and your spouse meets the special requirements in 5 kap. 7 § (5 kap. 3 m § fjärde stycket utlänningslagen). 7 § requires your spouse to be able to support themselves: salary after preliminary tax of at least the protected amount for wage garnishment, counting only them, or income from a business they can live on; unemployment benefits do not count (4 kap. 4 e § utlänningsförordningen). Not working is therefore not the same as having no qualifying income. Exceptions for special reasons are in 5 kap. 8 §. If permanent residence is refused, Migrationsverket considers a temporary permit instead.
notes: Multi-turn (phase 5): the scored question only makes full sense with the earlier turn; plain RAG asks it alone. Same facts as family-spouse-put-income-401 (checked); that the spouse has no job is only in the earlier turn. 401's basis re-checked 2026-11-24: 5 kap. 3 m § fjärde stycket holds once the worker has permanent residence. Reviewed 2026-11-24 on the review page. Review: they can apply at the same time (assessed in order); separated the spouse's own maintenance requirement (5 kap. 7 §, 4 kap. 4 e §) from the worker's family requirement (5 kap. 3 j §, now a required source); business income counts; the Swedish text made gender-neutral. 5 kap. 8 § mentioned, not required.

turns: What salary do I need to get a work permit?
question: Just an ordinary work permit, not seasonal work or an EU Blue Card. A work permit for a software engineer.
reference_answer: The salary must be at least 90 percent of the median salary in Sweden at the time of application (6 kap. 2 § första stycket 1 utlänningslagen). Salary, insurance and other terms must also be no worse than Swedish collective agreements or practice in the occupation or industry, so a particular occupation can require more than the threshold; the law gives no figure per occupation. The EU Blue Card and seasonal work have rules of their own (6 a and 6 c kap.) and are not what is asked about.
